title: "Getting Started"

This is a sample page demonstrating what Quarto can do.

## Markdown basics

You get all the usual markdown features — headings, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, etc.

## Code blocks with syntax highlighting

```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
Use callouts to highlight important information.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Or to warn about common pitfalls.
:::

## Interactive example

Below is a live, interactive element using Observable JS — users can tweak inputs and see results update in real time:

```{ojs}
viewof name = Inputs.text({label: "Your name", placeholder: "World", value: "World"})
```

```{ojs}
md`**Hello, ${name}!** 👋`
```

```{ojs}
viewof count = Inputs.range([1, 50], {step: 1, value: 10, label: "How many items?"})
```

```{ojs}
md`You selected **${count}** items.`
```

## Tabbed content

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
for i in range(10):
    print(i)
```

### JavaScript

```javascript
for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
  console.log(i);
}
```

### Haskell

```haskell
mapM_ print [0..9]
```

:::

## Diagrams

```{mermaid}
graph LR
    A[Read docs] --> B[Try it out]
    B --> C{Understand?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Ship it]
    C -->|No| A
```

## Adding new pages

1. Create a new `.qmd` file in the project root
2. Add it to the navbar in `_quarto.yml`
3. Push — GitHub Actions will rebuild and deploy automatically
